title: The One Best Strategy For Difficult And Challenging Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that no single behavior tool — rewards, contracts, praise, rapport, or even direct accountability — comes close to the influence of an overall classroom culture built through expert classroom management. His claim is that once a teacher creates a genuinely well-run, hardworking, well-behaved class, peer pressure from that culture exerts more power over difficult students than any individual intervention, causing them to gradually mimic the behavior, posture, and work habits of their classmates. He is explicit that this only works if the teacher is not merely good but truly excellent at classroom management, capable of building the kind of intrinsically motivated 'team' culture associated with elite coaches. He directly challenges the assumption that some students with labels like ADHD or impulse-control issues are simply unreachable, arguing instead that they may just be waiting for the right environment, and closes with a call to abandon a scattershot mix of temporary tricks in favor of the unified, synergistic SCM approach, which he notes is free and available in the site's archive.
points: No single tool — rewards, contracts, praise, or rapport — matches the influence of an overall classroom culture built through excellent classroom management.
Once a genuinely well-run, hardworking classroom culture is established, peer pressure from that culture becomes the strongest force shaping even the most difficult students.
The effect requires the teacher to be excellent, not merely adequate, at classroom management — comparable to elite team-building coaches.
Labels like ADHD or impulse-control issues are reframed as burdens some students may be waiting for the right environment to shed, not fixed limitations.
A unified, synergistic approach to classroom management is presented as more effective than a scattershot mix of temporary behavioral tricks.
quotes: There is one strategy that works better than all others combined.
Because, you see, your class, and the way they behave collectively, has far greater power and influence over difficult and challenging students than you ever will.
However, there is one caveat to the strategy: You can’t be just good at classroom management. It will help, for sure, but it won’t promise actual change.
Maybe, or maybe these are just labels they’ve been carrying around with them like a leaden backpack, just waiting for someone or something to remove their burden.
SCM is a unified approach, whereby everything you do makes everything else easier and more effective.
